questions.question:
Which part of the fruit, labeled in the given figure makes it a false fruit?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f8580fba166ef01802976b98cc0db0e1304b7f501ed9cbd76f25f71e0952288c.png] [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/312136c86e88e0a4ee4a941f9fe34a0173bce96b4ef0c453839203d7b5e92c03.png]
questions.solution:
__Concept: __

__
 
• Fruit refers to a **mature** or **ripened ovary**, developed after **fertilization**.
 
• The fruit consists of a wall or **pericarp and seeds.**
 
• When the **pericarp is thick and fleshy**, it is differentiated into the **outer epicarp**, the **middle mesocarp,** and the** inner endocarp**. 

Explanation__:

__
 
• 
 
Fruit is said to be false fruit when the fruit is formed from the other parts of the flower as well as the ovary like **the receptacle (base), the perianth, thalamus, inflorescence, or calyx.**

 
 
• 
 
Examples of such fruits are **strawberries, pineapple, mulberry, apples, pears, etc.**

 
 
• 
 
The given figure is of a** false fruit.**

 
 
• 
 
False fruit develops from other floral parts and the thalamus along with the development of the ovary wall.

 
 
• **Therefore, the correct answer is option 4.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** If the fruit is formed** without fertilization of the ovary**, it is called a** parthenocarpic fruit**.

questions.question:
Identify the given structure.

questions.solution:
**Correct Answer: 2)**

**__Concept__**: 

__
 
• Nitrogenous bases are the organic compounds that contain nitrogen and are involved in the basic structure of nucleic acids (DNA and RNA).
 
• 5 types of nitrogen bases are there - **adenine, thymine, uracil, cytosine, and guanine.**
 
• In **DNA adenine, thymine, guanine, and cytosine** are present while in **RNA adenine, uracil, guanine, and cytosine.**
 
• Nitrogenous bases are further divided into purines (double ring str. -** adenine and guanine)** and pyrimidines (single ring structure - **uracil, cytosine, and thymine).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/277cc94373480197821c7eb0ee87398509411e579d94a63b9e02bc48686ad8ab.png] [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/512d52fd7d0589b9eb80eaea96e65cb37aeb5dd93a8d82673a108e5a10f69f62.png] [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8cb42050a2a524fb6d35dcce94dc6717f6d76d9acd04cc728cafd4e5ec96fef9.png] [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/31acd0f05a31a793337e48fcae295c5248c6b68b00de680b5dec75cf6b5b7ae2.png] [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6e6c679222ce936ba0c628dc62962cfa95e889bae1316bd3e9b50ea47d8be322.png] 

**Explanation__****:**

**Option 1: **Adenylic acid– **INCORRECT**

 
• **An adenylic acid is a form of adenine when phosphoric acid is added to it. Adenine is a purine and has a double ring structure.**
 
• Hence this option is incorrect.

Option 2: Uracil– CORRECT

 
• **Uracil is a nitrogenous base found in RNA and is a pyrimidine and the given structure is of uracil.**
 
• Hence this option is correct.

Option 3: Cholesterol – INCORRECT

 
• **Cholesterol has a sterol nucleus and hydrocarbon tail.**
 
• Hence this option is incorrect.

Option 4: Adenosine – INCORRECT

 
• **Adenosine is a nucleotide i.e., adenine with sugar and phosphate.**
 
• Hence this option is incorrect.

So, the correct answer is an **option (2).**

questions.solution:
__Concept:__

Dehydration reaction of alcohols:

__
 
• Alcohols when heated at high temperatures in presence of conc acids, undergo dehydration.
 
• They lose a molecule of water and form alkenes.
 
• The reaction proceeds via a carbocationic intermediate.
 
• The ease of dehydration follows the order tertiary>secondary>primary.
 
• There is a formation of unexpected products because the rearrangement of carbocations takes place in the reaction.
 
• Carbocationic rearrangement takes place whenever there is a possibility of a more stable intermediate to be formed by rearrangement.
 
• More stable carbonation gives a more saturated alkene as the product.

Explanation:__

 
• In the first step, the nucleophilic oxygen of the OH group of alcohol takes up a proton from the acid.
 
• In the next step elimination of water molecule takes place and gives the carbocationic intermediate. 
 
• In the third step Rearrangement of this intermediate takes place to give a more stable carbocation.
 
• Finally, elimination of proton occurs giving more substituted alkenes.
 
• The mechanism is:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/df882a43a789f7d23980446dc29bb6ca409fce4cd4bc2a2aaffca9fe394466c0.png]

The current (I)-Voltage (v) plot of a certain electronic device is given above. The device is:

options.text: a conductor which obeys Ohm's law

questions.solution:
__Concept:__

__
 
• Ohm’s law: The Current through the metallic element is directly proportional to the potential difference when the temperature remains constant.

 
• I ∝ V or V ∝ I or V = IR [where v= potential difference, I = current, R = resistance].
 
• Ohm’s law is not a universal law, the substances, which obey ohm’s law are known as ohmic substance. e.g. aluminium, copper, silver conductors etc.
 
• The substance which do not obey ohm’s law are non-ohmic substance e.g. gases, crystal rectifiers, thermionic valves, transistors, semiconductors, diode, bulb filaments etc.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/97b67a87cd1488bbae78c3f34603934f68c33ee07ae902c883a2a6924c3e9243.png] 

 
• If the graph between current (I) and Voltage (V) is a straight line, they obey ohm’s law.
 
• The non-ohmic resistors shows curve in graph.

**
Explanation:__

 
• The given devices are –
 
 
• Conducting copper coil – ohmic object
 
• Electric heating coil – heating coils are of metals – ohmic device
 
• Semiconductor diode – Non-ohmic in nature
 
• Rheostat – multiple copper coils are of copper metal – ohmic instrument
 
 

Hence the above-given graph is of conductor obey ohm's law**

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **A- Selaginella B- Gingko**

__**Explanation:**__

 
• Plants given in the figure are A - Selaginella and B- Ginkgo respectively.
 
• **Selaginella **is a trailing, hanging or erect evergreen lycopod (**Pteridophyte**). Selaginella plant body is sporophyte and differentiated into roots, stems, and leaves.
 
 
• Leaves are dimorphic (small and big).
 
• Small leaves are present on the dorsal side of the stem and bigger ones on the ventral side of the stem.
 
• The smaller leaves alternate with smaller ones and bigger leaves alternate with bigger ones.
 
• Selaginella has fertile leaves called sporophylls, which bear two types of sporangia – microsporangia and megasporangia.
 
 
 
• ***Ginkgo biloba** *belongs to the group of plants known as **gymnosperms**. 
 
 
• *Ginkgo biloba* has not changed for the last several millions of years since its appearance in triassic period.
 
• It is also called **living fossil**.
 
• The plant has survived due to interest shown by horticulturists. It has natural immunity to several plant diseases.

questions.question:
Find the resistance of the conductor using the given graph.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/94a6b68c98a9c172298e425de1c497fae72613aedc1a7d7c234233143a7827bd.png]
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** 60 ohm.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Resistance **is the opposition offered by a conductor to the flow of current through it.
 
• In the given graph, we can see that the** current is directly proportional **to the voltage.
 
• This means that the resistance of the conductor is** constant,** i.e., it does not change with the change in voltage or current.
 
• To find the resistance of the conductor, we need to use **Ohm's law**, which states that resistance (R) is equal to voltage (V) divided by current (I), i.e., R = V/I.
 
• From the graph, we can see that the voltage is **12V **and the current is** 0.2A.**
 
• Therefore, the resistance of the conductor is R = V/I = 12/0.2 = **60 ohm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The German physicist Georg **Simon Ohm **was the first to empirically validate Ohm's law.
 
• The resistance constant, R, in the equation **V=IR**, is measured in ohms and is denoted by the symbol **Ω.**
 
• Only when the given** temperature** and the other** physical parameters** stay **constant **does Ohm's law apply.
 
• In some components, the temperature **rises** when the current is **increased.**
 
• A **light bulb's filament **serves as an illustration of this, wherein increasing current causes the filament's temperature to rise.
 
• Ohm's law** cannot be** applied in this situation.
 
• The filament of the lightbulb **defies Ohm's Law. **
